properties.chose: All six rules, as written, made official by Anthony on 2026-09-27: "I'd like to accept the 6 rules as official. Let's reverse the 07-25 rule - let's retire sharing design through git." (1) One design per design: the store of the server that serves it. (2) Sharing is shared access to that server. (3) An export is a copy at one moment that reflow2 never tracks, refreshes or compares. (4) reflow2 works only from the design, and an export comes back only by an explicit import that replaces it. (5) Taking an export to another server is a fork. (6) Backup is of stores, periodic and across all designs. Open question (a) answered with it: git-carried sharing is retired for ALL designs, not only served ones; dec:multi-writer-architecture is superseded. Questions (b) CI against a design on a server, (c) per-branch implementation facts, and (d) a perishable stamp on an export stay open. How people share a design is a separate brainstorm: dec:idea-how-does-somebody-share-a-reflow2-design.
properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, dev_reflow2 hub session, 2026-09-27, stepping back after a day of export problems (the hub cannot watch cure on flo2.io; an agent in cure's folder would be served the frozen laptop store; removing the export would break flo2's and reflow2's CI and PR flow):

"In taking a step back, I want just one "blueprint". I believe that blueprint lives inside the reflow2 mcp storage in the rocksdb (is that a correct assumption?). What I want to occur: if we have a shared reflow2 mcp (like flo2.io offers), another user can (if the blueprint is shared) go there and make changes to the design (doesn't need the photocopy of the blueprint at all). Now if the user wants to get a copy of the real blueprint (our photocopy), the only way they could use it is if they wanted to use it with another reflow2 mcp server (in this case, not flo2.io's reflow2 mcp). In that case, the user can either delete the one on flo2.io or accept that the photocopy and the one on flo2.io will diverge. I think that is the only use case of a photocopy (which I think may be the exported reflow2 design json). If it is the export of design, I think this should be a perishable product, meaning that once it it produced, the reflow2 mcp is not responsible for tracking it that it is updated and in sync with the real blueprint. If the user wants to take photocopies often, that's cool, but reflow2 will only use the real blueprint - unless the user states, go back and use the photocopy, but reflow2 will then import that into reflow2 rocksdb and that replaces the real blueprint and becomes the new real blueprint. Now for the real blueprint, which I believe is in the rocksdb, we may want to back that up in case the reflow2 mcp crashes. This may also take the form of exporting the designs periodically, though rocksdb probably has a better way to backup it's contents periodically. This would be more a mass export versus design by design, I'd imagine"

═══ THE IDEA AS SIX RULES (a restatement for reading, his words above govern) ═══
1. ONE DATA STORE per design: the store of the reflow2 server that serves it.
2. SHARING is shared access to that server. No copy moves between people.
3. AN EXPORT IS A COPY AT ONE MOMENT: made on request, never tracked, refreshed or compared by reflow2.
4. reflow2 WORKS ONLY FROM THE DESIGN. An export comes back only by an explicit import that REPLACES the design.
5. TAKING AN EXPORT TO ANOTHER SERVER IS A FORK: delete the original, or accept that the two diverge.
6. BACKUP IS OF DESIGNS, periodic and store-level across all designs, not a per-design export.

═══ HIS QUESTION, ANSWERED FROM THE CODE ═══
YES. A design is a RocksDB store (reflow2-core's `rocksdb` feature, always on in reflow2-mcp): locally at <folder>/.reflow2/graph, on flo2.io one store per design under /srv/flo2/designs/<design>/.reflow2/graph. Two riders: the store has sidecars beside it (graph.id.json is the design's identity; a store opened without it presents as EMPTY, per dec:backup-belongs-to-the-consumer), and it carries its search index. rule 1 therefore means the store directory with its sidecars.

═══ HOW THE EXPORT BECAME LOAD-BEARING (history, measured from the record) ═══
- 2026-07-21 dec:export-hash-chain: the committed export gains a tamper-evident chain because "the committed export file IS the durable record whose lineage matters".
- 2026-07-25 dec:multi-writer-architecture (ACCEPTED): many writers "keep the repo file and merge on pull — no hosted service". Each person's design lives in their own checkout and git moves it. THIS is where the export became the medium people share.
- Built on it: the CI gate reads the committed export (BL-66); one export per PR (08-01); req:stale-seat-knows calls the live store "a long-lived cache of the committed design export"; the dependency watch (08-26); the server writes the export through on every change (09-11, to make "the git record reliable"); git-mergeable saved design (09-22).
- 2026-09-11: making the export the truth was REJECTED and RocksDB kept durable, which is rule 1. But the write-through was kept for git's sake, so the export stayed tracked.
- 2026-09-24..26: flo2.io hosts designs, the option 07-25 rejected. dec:multi-writer-architecture was never re-opened. req:persistence was dropped, and its replacement (req:a-design-lives-in-its-server-not-in-the-code-repo) is still proposed.
⇒ Two models run side by side: git carries the export (reflow2, flo2) and the server holds the design (cure). Every export problem found on 2026-09-26/27 sits on the seam between them.

═══ WHAT IT WOULD OVERTURN OR RESCOPE, IF CHOSEN ═══
- dec:multi-writer-architecture (accepted): reversed. The hosted service becomes how many people work one design.
- The move decision's clause "the repo's export becomes a copy the local client writes back" (settled 09-25): withdrawn.
- req:the-server-keeps-the-working-tree-export-current and the 09-11 write-through: become optional ("export on every change, if you like"), never read back.
- req:stale-seat-knows, dec:export-once-per-pr, req:the-saved-design-merges-correctly-under-gits-ordinary-merge, dec:export-hash-chain (file lineage): lose their subject for served designs. Design history already has a git-free home in dec:the-designs-lineage-is-kept-per-item.
- The dependency watch and the hub: a child is watched by asking its server (address), never a file.

═══ WHAT IT COSTS, recorded beside it (not arguing it down) ═══
- 🛑 THE CODE STILL NEEDS CHECKING AGAINST THE DESIGN. Today CI checks the code against the export (registered files, their fingerprints, open gaps). Under rule 3 CI must ask the design: network access and a credential from CI, which is req:results-from-the-code-flow-back-into-a-design-that-lives-elsewhere (proposed) and unbuilt. Until it exists, a served design has no design check in CI.
- DESIGN CHANGES LEAVE THE PR DIFF. A reviewer no longer sees design and code change side by side. An export committed with a PR could still be shown, as a record nothing reads.
- ONE DESIGN, MANY CODE BRANCHES. Code has branches and a design does not. Facts that belong to one branch (req:implementation-facts-travel-with-the-branch-that-produced-them: file fingerprints on a feature branch) need a home in the store, not in a branch's export. Open.
- "WORK NEEDS SOMETHING I CAN GIT COMMIT" (Anthony and Alex, 09-25, req:the-design-saves-itself-wherever-the-owner-chooses) is compatible: commit exports as records; reflow2 just never reads them back.
- LOCAL-ONLY STAYS WHOLE (req:reflow2-keeps-working-entirely-on-one-machine): a local server's store is that design. What goes is git as the way two people share one design without a server; they would share a server instead (flo2.io, an organisation's own, or `--serve-shared` on their network).
- A FROZEN STORE LEFT BY A MOVE is, under rule 5, a second design on another server. The owner deletes it or keeps it knowingly, and reflow2 must not open it as the design when the folder points elsewhere (fact:an-agent-opened-in-a-moved-designs-folder-is-served-the-frozen-store-2026-09-27).

═══ BACKUP (rule 6), measured ═══
flo2 does rule 6 today: nightly, every design, by STOPPING the reflow2 container (~10 s) and tarring the RocksDB directories plus flo2's Postgres dump, then pulling off-box and pushing encrypted to Spaces. It stops the server because reflow2's --export-snapshot is "NOT crash-consistent … never a backup" (cap:snapshot-read), and "the durable alternative upstream would prefer isn't exposed yet" (flo2 ops/README.md). RocksDB's own answer is a CHECKPOINT: a consistent, online, near-instant copy of a live store. reflow2 does not expose one. dec:backup-belongs-to-the-consumer (accepted) already draws the line: running backups is the operator's job, and reflow2 owes "honest primitives". A consistent online snapshot of every store a server holds would be that primitive, and "mass rather than design-by-design" is then one command looping over the stores.

═══ OPEN QUESTIONS THIS LEAVES ═══
(a) Re-open dec:multi-writer-architecture for SERVED designs only, or for all? Is git-carried sharing kept for anyone?
(b) How does CI check local code against a design on a server?
(c) Where do per-branch implementation facts live when the design has no branches?
(d) Does an export carry anything that marks it perishable (a "taken from <server>/<id> at <time>, not tracked" stamp), so no reader mistakes it for live?

═══ 2026-09-27, LATER — THE FOUR OPEN QUESTIONS ABOVE ARE ALL ANSWERED ═══
(a) Git-carried sharing is retired for ALL designs (Anthony; chg:sharing-a-design-through-git-is-retired-2026-09-27).
(b) CI checks code against the design on its server: req:ci-checks-the-code-against-its-design-on-the-server (accepted), with req:results-from-the-code-flow-back-into-a-design-that-lives-elsewhere (accepted the same day).
(c) Per-branch implementation facts live in the store with their branch: req:implementation-facts-travel-with-the-branch-that-produced-them, accepted 2026-09-22 and found to answer this already.
(d) Every export says it is one: req:a-photocopy-says-it-is-one (accepted).
The order in which all of this lands is the tracked-export retirement plan, epochs planned-v0720-the-remote-client-is-released through planned-flo2-then-reflow2-move-and-the-export-retires, confirmed by Anthony on 2026-09-27. Backups without stopping the server (rule 6) is req:a-server-offers-a-consistent-live-snapshot-of-every-store, outside that order.
properties.name: SETTLED 2026-09-27 — one design: a design IS its server's store, people share it by sharing that server, an export is a copy at one moment reflow2 never tracks, and importing one replaces the design; sharing through git is retired
properties.rationale: Captured as brainstorming because it re-opens an accepted architecture decision and retires or rescopes several accepted requirements. Only Anthony can settle it, and he has not yet seen the costs set out. The history is recorded with it because his question was "how did we arrive here", and the answer (git as the sharing medium, chosen 07-25, never re-opened when flo2.io began hosting) is what makes the six rules a reversal rather than an addition.
